correctness.rationale: Writing \(x=|S\cap A|\) and \(y=|S\cap B|\), the switched graph has the explicit bipartition \((S\cap A)\cup(B\setminus S)\) and \((S\cap B)\cup(A\setminus S)\), hence is \(K_{b+x-y,a-x+y}\). Equality of unordered part sizes with \(\{a,b\}\) gives exactly \(x-y=0\) or \(a-b\). Vandermonde counts each selector family, with coincidence exactly in the balanced case. In \(K_{2,3}\), a singleton in the larger part and an edge containing it are both identity switches, while their symmetric difference is a singleton in the smaller part and is not. The frozen verifier independently exhausts all selectors in 33 small parameter cases.
correctness.risk: The exact selector enumeration may have an older equivalent formulation in switching-class literature under different terminology.

final_claim: For \(K_{a,b}\), a selector \(S\) is an identity Seidel switch exactly when \(|S\cap A|-|S\cap B|\in\{0,a-b\}\); the exact selector count is \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) when \(a=b\) and twice that when \(a\ne b\), and \(K_{2,3}\) gives a counterexample to the published subgroup-closure assertion.
limitations: No general classification of identity-switch families is claimed.
